Mark has toured bouffon shows internationally, and Alice produces festivals such as: Mothers Who Make and Clownfest MCR. They both teach on The Performers' Playground course, and have had successful artistic and teaching careers.


But five years ago, Mark was diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis (MS)... so how does someone who is a physical performer continue to explore and develop their work whilst navigating a disruptive central nervous system, affecting cognition, and developing a funny walk, and how does Alice help, support and sustain a balanced family life, career whilst making this show!


In each episode, we talk to the cast and crew to discover what it's like making a bouffon show (a theatre fringe genre only tackled by the bravest); what it’s like to navigate through political unrest whilst tackling a highly political play; AND why Mark (even with MS) is still the most annoying cast member…

In this series, Crawlspace Media's Tim Pilleri and Lance Reenstierna speak with Worcester State University archives librarian Ross Griffiths to break down each individual case and come to the most likely conclusion. In the final episode, Tim, Lance, and Ross speak with Joseph Citro, the author and Vermont folklorist who coined the term "Bennington Triangle".

description:
StarFans Podcast

In the years before basketball cards blew up, a small company called Star printed the very first cards of Michael Jordan and a whole generation of legends, including Dominique Wilkins, Clyde Drexler and Charles Barkley.

Star collectors have been quietly hooked for forty years. Since 2022, the secret’s been getting out. The questions are bigger than ever: What did Star make? How many are out there? And what’s still hiding in an attic, a shoebox, or a sealed bag?

StarFans is documenting the Star basketball universe, one bag, one card, one story at a time. Host Sean Campbell sits down with the collectors, historians and lifelong fans who’ve spent decades piecing it together, swapping finds and the stories that never made it into the price guides.

The cards are rarely perfectly centered. Neither are the conversations, and that’s the best part. Pull up a chair. You’re among friends.

description:
A guerra já não chega só como guerra. Chega como um incêndio num armazém, um boato que se espalha antes do almoço, uma queixa a um regulador, um cabo danificado no fundo do mar. A maioria dessas coisas tem uma explicação inocente. Algumas não têm.
Quando não têm, o alvo raramente é o Estado diretamente. É a sociedade. E o caminho mais curto até ela passa pelas empresas: a de energia, a operadora, o banco, o supermercado. É ali que a vida cotidiana acontece, e é ali que a pressão é aplicada. Um apagão, um serviço que não volta, uma marca de confiança copiada para espalhar mentiras. O objetivo não é a empresa. É o que as pessoas passam a sentir, a pensar e a decidir por causa do que aconteceu com ela.
Terreno Firme é sobre essa pressão e o que ela faz. Como os adversários pensam o conflito abaixo do limiar da guerra. Como a informação e a percepção se tornam armas. Como empresas, instituições e sociedades se mantêm de pé, e o que é preciso para decidir quando ninguém vai dizer que é seguro. Alguns episódios são práticos. Outros são de análise. Todos terminam no que isso significa para você, seja você gestor, funcionário ou simplesmente cidadão.
Jānis Bērziņš introduziu o conceito de guerra de nova geração no Ocidente e estuda a guerra híbrida e cognitiva russa há mais de uma década. Ele concebe e conduz simulações de crise e jogos de guerra sobre como governos e empresas respondem sob pressão.

Like sewing, storytelling brings together different materials, perspectives, and people into something whole. Meaningful work is done one stitch at a time, with care, patience, and intention, creating a blanket woven from the voices of our people.

Welcome to MrYouWho – Real Products, Real Tests, Real Reviews, hosted by Andrew Hough.

From headphones, speakers and home entertainment to AI software, smart home technology, robotic cleaners, solar power systems and the latest gadgets, we put products and software to the test in real-world conditions.

title: VR Barnes
author: Violet Rebecca
description:
Violet Rebecca Barnes

Science fiction promised us flying cars, silver jumpsuits, and dinner in a pill—and honestly, none of that sounded very comfortable anyway. Welcome to VR Barnes, where host Violet Rebecca Barnes skips the gloomy robot-apocalypse stories to look at the genuinely good, helpful, and wonderfully human things tomorrow is bringing into our lives. From clever home helpers that let our grandparents stay in their own kitchens, and medicine that actually knows your name, to quieter streets, fixable toasters, and ways to keep your brain calm in a world full of screens, this is your cheerful guide to the decades ahead. Grab a cup of coffee, leave the doom-scrolling at the door, and let us talk about why the future is looking a lot brighter—and much more livable—than the movies told us.

title: The Art Of Health with Dr. Lisa Smaldone
author: DAC Productions LLC
description:
The Art of Health with Dr. Lisa Smaldone, M.D.

Real conversations, real answers, a healthier you, brighter tomorrows.

Good health is more than just medicine. It's about making informed choices, feeling your best, and enjoying a healthier, more fulfilling life.

Join Dr. Lisa Smaldone, M.D., for engaging, down-to-earth conversations exploring the many dimensions of health, wellness, and longevity. From nutrition, fitness, weight management, and healthy aging to hormones, energy, preventative care, and the latest developments in medicine, The Art of Health brings meaningful health discussions into everyday life.

Through expert insights, special guests, real-life experiences, and honest conversations, Dr. Lisa breaks down complex health topics into practical information you can understand and use.

Whether you're looking to improve your health, stay active, better understand your body, or simply make smarter choices for the future, The Art of Health offers knowledge, encouragement, and a fresh perspective on living well.

Because it's not just about living longer. It's about living better.

Join us in our fun convos and let's go on a ride.

Healthcare doesn't have to sound clinical. It can be evidence-based and entertaining. Professional and playful. Educational and deeply human.

Know more. Feel more. Do more!

author: Ryan McNally
description: Living longer is only half the battle — the real goal is thriving for as long as possible. Expedition Healthspan is a conversation from the frontier of longevity: what the research actually says about exercise, sleep, food, hormones, and the biology of aging, explained in plain English by clinician Ryan McNally, ND, PA, who goes straight to the researchers and clinicians producing that research — and translates dense clinical science into everyday habits. Short, digestible episodes built for real life — no hype, no product pitches, just the science and what to do with it. Your journey starts here.

title: 3T THE PODCAST
author: Alphonso
description:
3T THE PODCAST is a survivor-led space built for truth, healing, and real-life transformation. Hosted by Alphonso Pelt alongside co-host Storm, 3T creates a judgment-free environment where survivors of childhood abuse and trauma can feel seen, understood, and supported without being talked down to or treated like a case study. Each episode blends structured, practical insight with raw, honest conversation—because healing is not a performance, it is a process, and nobody should have to do it alone.

At its core, 3T THE PODCAST exists to help people move from surviving to rebuilding with clarity, boundaries, and self-respect. We talk about trauma responses, family dynamics, recovery tools, and the long-term impact of abuse across every stage of life, while keeping the message grounded and actionable for both survivors and the people who love them. This is your reminder that self-care is not selfish, community matters, and liberation is possible—one honest step at a time.

Search Takeover™ — Dominate Your Information Environment.

Modern life gives us more choice, comfort and opportunity than ever before. But is it actually making us happier?
Modern Human is a podcast exploring what it means to live well in the modern world.
Through open, honest conversations with people from all walks of life, we explore the big questions around happiness, purpose, relationships, work, identity and what it means to be human.
No blueprints, perfect answers or five-step formulas. Just curiosity, different perspectives and a willingness to question what we've been taught about success and living a good life.

title: The Unspoken Cost of Cancer Podcast
author: Brett Wilson
description:
Cancer’s costs reach far beyond the medical bills.
The Unspoken Cost Podcast, hosted by Brett Wilson, founder and CEO of Walking Miracles Family Foundation and a two-time childhood cancer survivor, brings those often-overlooked burdens into the conversation.
From travel expenses and missed work to emotional exhaustion, strained relationships, and the lasting effects of treatment, this podcast explores what cancer means for patients, survivors, caregivers, and families—during treatment and long afterward.

title: Prey Tell
author: Ashley Schef
description:
PREY TELL is a true crime podcast built with the belief that the victim is the story, not the sensationalized predator. Every victim has a story to tell, and that story deserves to be told. The naming of Prey Tell is a nod to the victims. Calling someone prey is what victims are reduced to when our society and legal system labels them as a case number and neglects to remember the real human suffering. My intention is to help reclaim that word for every victim. Because in every episode, I’ll examine a case and hunt for the truth.

 

New episodes drop every week. You can subscribe now wherever you get your podcasts, and find the show across social media platforms @preytellpodcast.

description:
History is stranger than you think! Join archaeologists and history creators Natasha Billson and Emily Harriss as they dig into the weird, wonderful and sometimes downright disturbing stories of the past.
Not So Ancient History explores the history you probably didn't learn at school. Expect fascinating discoveries, historical mysteries, a little myth-busting and plenty of laughs along the way.
Because the past is never quite what it seems.

From business practices and industry politics to safety, leadership, and the realities of running trucks, he challenges conventional thinking and asks the questions worth answering.
Expect candid opinions, practical experience, and a willingness to question the way things have always been done. Industry politics may be part of the conversation, but they don't set the agenda.

Leadership advice is everywhere. Evidence is harder to find. Subject to Evidence cuts through the noise to explore what actually works in leading organisations, from setting strategy to running meetings that matter.

Each season takes one big question about leadership and management and works through it episode by episode, drawing on research, real-world practice and hard-won lessons. Season 1 explores strategic leadership: what it is, why it so often fails, and how leaders can do it well. Season 2 tackles meetings, from everyday catch-ups to the strategic sessions that shape an organisation’s future.

Made for executives, managers, board members and anyone responsible for getting things done through people, Subject to Evidence offers practical, clear-eyed insight you can use the next time you walk into a room.

New episodes every Monday and Wednesday.

Subject to Evidence is a podcast by Lantern (lanterncorp.com.au), helping organisations strategise with purpose and prove their impact.

Subject to Evidence is made by people and uses some AI working together. Conversations feature both human and AI hosts

The Midnight Files is a horror and mystery podcast bringing you chilling true stories, unexplained encounters, terrifying experiences, strange disappearances, disturbing mysteries, dark folklore, and fictional tales that will make you question what’s hiding in the shadows.

From encounters that happened in the dead of night to mysteries that have never been solved, each episode takes you deeper into the unknown.

We're committed to funding and encouraging industry-related study and research through scholarships, endowments, and donations. 

Join us as we discuss innovative research projects, share success stories of Australians who have benefitted from our support, and learn from leaders who are pioneering new advancements. title: "from the inside  out
author: María
description: What happens when the dream you hold in your hands clashes with the future your family wants for you?In this 10-minute episode, I share a deeply personal story: the intrapersonal conflict between starting my own traditional handicraft and weaving venture — the techniques my grandmother taught me — and my family's expectation that I find a stable, 9-to-5 job.What started as a silent dilemma inside me — excitement, fear, guilt, and hope — began to spill over. It made me defensive at the dinner table, impatient at home, and quick to argue with friends and neighbors.In this reflective analysis, I explore how an inner struggle can become family tension, interpersonal conflict, and even affect community coexistence. Drawing on Duque (2010), Quiroga (2023), Dragomir (2024), Rincón (2022, 2023), and Villarán (2025) on the Golden Rule of Ethics, I show how I moved from avoidance and competition to compromise and collaboration — finding a path that honored both my need for purpose and my family's need for security.Key takeaway: Peace doesn't start in public squares or institutions. It starts inside each of us, is strengthened in the family, and then spreads to the entire community.Perfect for students of psychology, social work, and anyone torn between following their passion and meeting family expectations.

title: What Should You Do When Cyberbullying Happens?
author: Precious Khaiseb
description:
Episode 3: "What Should You Do When Cyberbullying Happens?"
Hi everyone, Today, we're sharing what to do when it happens.


Point one: don't fight back with bullying. Insulting them back only makes things worse and could get you in trouble too. Stay calm and don't reply.


Point two: save evidence. Take screenshots of the messages and posts, and note the dates and usernames. Don't delete anything, because proof helps others act.


Point three: block the bully. This stops them from messaging you or seeing your profile. It's protecting your peace, not running away.


Point four: report the account. Apps and platforms can remove harmful content or suspend the account, so use the report button.


Point five: tell a trusted adult, like a parent, teacher or school counsellor. Asking for help isn't weak. You don't have to face this alone.


Point six: know where to seek help. That could be your school, a social worker, a helpline, or the police if there are threats.


And a special thank you to anyone who has supported a friend going through cyberbullying. Your kindness makes a real difference.


This is the end of our three-episode series on cyberbullying. Stay safe online, be kind, and look out for each other.


Thank you, and goodbye!

description:
Welcome to No Matter, a brand design critique podcast of little consequence, by two experts. Nothing we say here will change a logo, but how we talk about design does matter.

In each episode, host Kaleb Dean and a fellow designer look at one rebrand: what works, what doesn't, and what's really at stake, financially, socially, and culturally. Our modality is to critique the work, not the people. We examine each rebrand with a keen eye and an open heart, uncovering the story behind it, decoding the design choices, and asking what they mean for the brand's identity.

From global corporations to local businesses, no rebrand is too big or too small, as long as there's something at stake beyond revenue. Expect candid conversation, expert insight, and a dash of humor, with the goal of modeling positive critique for the design world and every area of life that warrants it.

Whether you're a designer, a business owner, or just curious about branding, follow No Matter wherever you listen to podcasts, and watch the video version on YouTube to see the designs as we discuss them. Have a rebrand you want us to critique? Email kaleb@overmatter.design.

description:
NFNT Business is for the intentional listener.

Hosted by Gloria Aderinokun, CEO of Madison Avenue Support Services (MASS), Gary A. Royster, CEO of Je Transporte, and Fatima Disu, COO of MASS, the podcast focuses on the practical side of building and operating a small business, particularly in the federal contracting space.

Each episode provides actionable insight on how small businesses can succeed and maneuver within their industry, regardless of what it is, insurance, fashion, transportation, or the federal marketplace. While industries differ, the pressures of running a small business tend to be similar. Owners face the same types of decisions around growth, staffing, finances, risk, and responsibility.

The conversations are grounded in real operational experience rather than theory. Episodes explore how to position a business for opportunity, how to think through difficult decisions, and how to navigate the systems that shape your industry.

We are not consultants. We are actual small business owners who have gone through, are going through, and will go through shit. We have nothing to sell you.

This podcast is intended to serve as a repository of information drawn from real experience operating businesses. The goal is to share what we have learned so others can use it within their own industries.

title: (Self) Starting a New Job
author: Nellie Wirth
description:
You got the job. Now comes the part no one fully prepares you for: figuring out how to succeed in it.


Welcome to (Self) Starting a New Job, the podcast that helps you take the driver's seat in your own onboarding and create a more confident, connected, and fulfilling start in your new role.


Your company's new hire training is important, but it can't teach you everything you need to know about navigating workplace relationships, understanding company culture, managing self-doubt, building confidence, and figuring out how to make your mark.


Drawing on nearly 25 years of HR experience, I'll share practical insights, actionable strategies, and a fresh perspective on the mental, professional, and relationship sides of starting a new job. You'll learn how to shift unhelpful thinking, communicate effectively with your manager, build meaningful workplace relationships, clarify expectations, and take intentional steps toward becoming a valued contributor.


Through the Self-Onboarding for Success approach, you'll discover how to move beyond simply getting through your first few months to creating a strong foundation for long-term success, growth, and joy at work.

This isn't about replacing your employer's onboarding program or pretending every workplace is perfect. It's about recognizing what you can control, advocating for what you need, and taking ownership of the experience you're creating for yourself.


Whether you're navigating your first job, changing careers, or starting a new role after years of experience, you'll find practical guidance and resources to help you make the transition with greater clarity, confidence, and purpose.


Your employer hired you. Now it's time to onboard yourself for success.
